patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — 8x8 and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose 8x8 only if your buying job matches “Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24” rather than Vonage's shape. Choose Vonage only if your buying job matches “SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/” rather than 8x8's shape. Workflow advantage: 8x8 leans contact-center; Vonage leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — 8x8 and Vonage share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: 8x8 is Global UCaaS + contact-centre platform (8x8 Work / X Series) — Work X2 research floor ~$24/user/month annual; CC tiers custom/higher.; Vonage is SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo; Premium/Advanced higher..
- Company-size focus: 8x8 (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Vonage (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: 8x8-leaning contact-center vs Vonage-leaning —.
- Researched limits: 8x8 — Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Vonage — Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors.

Limitations — 8x8: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated; Mandatory regulatory/service fees frequently sit on top of list seats; Vonage: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors; Call recording and deeper CRM land on Advanced / Premium packaging.

Poor-fit cases: 8x8 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Published seat floors are medium confidence — first-party pricing often bot/quote gated · Vonage is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Taxes and regulatory fees sit on top of published per-line floors · Avoid 8x8 if you actually need Vonage's motion (SMB/mid VoIP business phone (VBC) — Mobile from $13.99/line/mo on 12-month promo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
